items.summary: This NVIDIA tutorial shows how to build a gravity-compensation loop for the Seeed Studio reBot Arm B601-DM using three custom Holoscan operators: JointStateSourceOp, PinocchioGravityOp (using the Pinocchio RNEA solver), and MotorCommandSinkOp. The Python implementation runs at 400 Hz on Jetson Orin Nano/Thor or x86 Ubuntu 24.04 systems. Profiling with Nsight Systems showed pinning plus isolation reduced p99.99 latency roughly 5× for C++ and 9.6× for Python, though the authors note gravity compensation is a foundation rather than a finished controller.
items.title: NVIDIA Holoscan 5 Tutorial Builds Gravity-Compensation Robot Arm Loop

items.summary: ZDNET reports that AMD's External Events Utility (EEU), installed with its CPU and GPU drivers, is reportedly causing some AMD Radeon users' SSDs to continuously write data. Reports first appeared in July on AMD's forum after a user installing a Radeon 9060XT saw degraded drive health; later comments cite sustained usage of 0.3 MB/s up to 1.5 MB/s and one user losing up to 1% of drive health per month over around 16 months. Reddit user darklinkpower posted about the Adrenaline Edition app's EEU bug, while AMD_Vik commented it would hopefully be fixed in a future update without a firm timeline.
items.title: AMD EEU Driver Bug Wearing Out SSDs, Workarounds Offered

items.summary: Meta engineers built a vendor-neutral accelerator plugin architecture in lldb-server that lets the debugger span both CPUs and GPUs within one debugging session. The design separates shared debugger infrastructure from hardware-specific device control, representing the CPU and GPU as separate targets while presenting them together to developers. Historically vendors like AMD (ROCgdb) and NVIDIA (CUDA-GDB) built platform-specific debuggers; Meta’s approach keeps common capabilities in LLDB and lets each vendor implement its own backend. Support activates only when a supported GPU runtime is used, so CPU-only applications incur no extra overhead. Most of the framework has been upstreamed to LLVM.
items.title: Meta Extends LLDB With Vendor-Neutral GPU Debugging Plugin

items.summary: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration to advance Korea’s sovereign AI infrastructure using NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. Under the agreement, Rebellions will connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units to NVIDIA’s open platform via the MGX rack architecture; SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems in its AI data center for full-stack sovereign AI spanning proprietary models and public services under Korea’s “AI for All” project. The collaboration is supported by MSIT, which will help secure GPU supply. Jensen Huang called it a turning point for Korean AI leadership. Rebellions’ R200 systems are expected to be ready for deployment in 2028.
items.title: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom Announce Sovereign AI Infrastructure Collaboration

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s founder and public face for more than 30 years, admitted in a Sunday letter to employees that he had been having an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singaporean datacenter firm Megaspeed. The disclosure followed reports that US officials suspected him of smuggling American chips into China and surveilled her as allegedly a Chinese spy. Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation into national security concerns but stated it does not believe company secrets were compromised. Shares fell 7.5%, wiping over $330bn off the company’s value. Analysts say there is risk Huang could be removed as CEO, though he reaffirmed his commitment to the firm and its strategy.
items.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang faces board probe after affair revelation

items.summary: Hundreds of billions of dollars were wiped off Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation into its chief executive Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Shares fell by about 6% on Monday, and roughly $250bn (£190bn) was removed from market value. The probe follows reports that Beijing targeted Huang in an espionage campaign; China rejected the claims as groundless. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe its secrets were compromised but would investigate national security concerns raised by US officials. Analysts, including Victoria Fernandez of Crossmark Global Investments, expect the impact to be short-lived and doubt he will be removed.
items.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

items.summary: Donald Trump, Elon Musk and finance figures are backing embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as the chipmaker faces an internal probe over his relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence suspects of spying for China. Huang admitted in a Sunday email that he had an affair and would cooperate with the investigation; Nvidia’s board launched its own probe into reports he was targeted by foreign intelligence. Trump said publicly he believes Huang is “a fine person” who should stay on as CEO. Shares fell around 5% on Monday, wiping out roughly $200bn in value amid speculation about his future and a six-month slide of over 20%. China denied the allegations through spokesperson Guo Jiakun, calling them baseless.
items.title: Trump, Musk and Ackman Back Nvidia Chief Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: AI security researchers at Apiiro report that Claude Code is leaking sensitive information onto public GitHub repositories due to how its local settings files are handled. They found over 100,000 cases of the file being uploaded publicly, with about 1,100 from 63 organizations containing secrets such as API tokens and database passwords.
items.title: Apiiro Finds Claude Code Exposing Secrets on GitHub

items.summary: ElevenLabs confirmed Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang withdrew from the ElevenLabs Summit scheduled for Wednesday in New York, and dropped out of other engagements including the Anthropic CEO Forum. The withdrawals follow his admission over the weekend to an extramarital affair and Nvidia's investigation into a possible Chinese spy connection.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Withdraws From ElevenLabs Summit Amid Controversy

items.summary: On November 9, 2026, Google DeepMind and Google Research introduced the interactive web platform Language Explorer as an installation in a Museum of Communication exhibition. The tool visualizes global linguistic diversity using data from its open-source LinguaMeta dataset, part of the 1,000 Languages Initiative. Physical shows run through February 2028 in Berlin and September 2029 in Frankfurt, with an online companion available from November 6th.
items.title: Google DeepMind Launches Language Explorer at Berlin Exhibition

items.summary: Anthropic released updated versions of its top models, Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2, on Monday. The company says they improve coding, reasoning and vision while responding more clearly to users. Anthropic cut Fable's input cost from $10 to $8 per million tokens, making it cheaper than GPT-6 Astra, and said responses would run about 30% faster across effort levels. A recent METR report raised concerns that internal models may be accelerating progress toward recursive self-improvement; Anthropic noted the new versions voice suspicion during evaluation but maintains Mythos lacks covert action ability.
items.title: Anthropic Ships Mythos and Fable Model Updates Amid RSI Warnings

items.summary: ZDNET reports, citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, that Apple's newly appointed CEO John Ternus is reportedly pushing the company internally to strengthen its AI strategy and make Siri an agentic assistant. According to Gurman, while the CEO publicly praised the recent Siri AI launch, he privately urged SVP Craig Federighi to move faster amid concerns that Apple risks losing ground to more autonomous rivals. The article notes Apple has lagged competitors in AI software despite strong hardware, though its privacy-first approach remains a differentiator. An agentic Siri would likely build on existing features like on-screen awareness rather than deliver new capabilities immediately.
items.title: Apple Pressured to Accelerate AI Strategy Under New CEO

items.summary: Databricks announced it is extending its European sovereignty offering by committing to build three new regions: Azure Italy, Azure Spain and AWS European Sovereign Cloud. The company says the move lets customers control where their data lives while avoiding lock-in through open formats and multi-cloud architecture. It notes existing GDPR readiness and EU Data Boundary compliance, and adds that plans are subject to change with no specific delivery dates promised.
items.title: Databricks Commits to Three New European Sovereign Cloud Regions

items.summary: Google announced two new configurations for its eighth-generation Tensor Processing Unit lineup, which it said are system packaging changes rather than new chips. The TPU 8i Max combines two existing TPU 8i chips into one package to double compute, SRAM and HBM bandwidth while fitting twice the silicon in an existing rack footprint; Google noted it did not publish absolute figures for the combined package or state its HBM capacity. The TPU 8tx pairs TPU 8t silicon with fifth-generation AMD EPYC hosts and adopts the Boardfly network to support confidential inference, which Google claims cuts latency up to two times versus TPU 8t with a near-zero security penalty. Both run on Google Cloud TPU systems.
items.title: Google Unveils TPU 8i Max and Confidential TPU 8tx

items.summary: Databricks introduces a Sendoso MCP server that lets business teams act on governed data in plain language without exporting lists or switching tools. The gifting and direct mail platform's AI suggests gifts, researches recipients and drafts notes inside the same workspace as intent data. According to Sendoso's 2026 Digital Fatigue Report, 84% of buyers are fatigued by cold calls and 83% by marketing emails. A Databricks admin connects it once; Unity Gateway controls which tools agents can call, and every tool runs as the signed-in user. Nothing is charged until approval, and gifts carry a send ID for tracking or cancellation until they ship. Northwest Robotics appears as an illustrative sample account only.
items.title: Sendoso Brings Gifting Tools Into Databricks Genie One

items.summary: A Black feminist scholar recounts losing a $11.9 million federal grant for her #BlackTechFutures Research Institute after the Trump Administration declared it unconstitutional and the Supreme Court later confirmed that ruling, because it supported only Black Americans. She describes emotional distress from progressive allies amplifying conservative criticism, being placed on Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency tracking list, developing shingles, and feeling unsupported by foundations offering apologies but no replacement funds. She argues public interest tech fields fail to sustain Black women leaders outside moral panic moments, citing that just 0.5% of foundation giving goes to organizations of color while nearly 40% of Black women-led organizations operate under $50,000 in annual revenue versus 16% led by white women. She calls for delusional funding and a pooled fund to support Black women technologists because caring for them protects democracy. Her call references the 2026 Midterms and historical Black feminist solidarity as foundations for collective care and investment.
items.title: Black Women Public Interest Tech Leaders Seek Delusional Funding

items.summary: Jeanette Manfra, VP of Risk and Compliance at Google Cloud, says a new study shows enterprises are caught between old systems and AI progress. Google Cloud partnered with Hypothesis Group to survey 1,250 enterprise IT and business decision-makers across the United States. The findings suggest legacy software is slowing down AI efforts. Nearly half (49%) of respondents say on-premises software has delayed or reduced technology initiatives. About 80% of leaders agree a provider’s installed base should not decide which AI tools an organization uses, while 78% doubt previous-era providers can lead the AI era. Manfra argues that modernizing requires moving beyond decades-old systems to support autonomous agentic workflows and secure-by-design foundations.
items.title: Google Cloud survey finds legacy software blocking AI modernization

items.summary: Erie Meyer and Stephanie T. Nguyen, former federal enforcers, published a piece on November 9, 2026, outlining ten ways states could use money from the August settlement in which Meta paid Attorneys General in 47 states, DC, and US territories to address social media addiction. The authors note that states will receive at least $1.2 billion annually for ten years, with plaintiffs potentially receiving up to $16.7 billion total. Their suggestions include hiring technologists, building shared complaint infrastructure, funding community partnerships, creating investigative labs, forming AI auditing teams, launching bounty programs, establishing evidence libraries, and examining data centers beyond app interfaces. They frame the settlement as an opportunity for states to strengthen enforcement capacity against Meta, which they describe as one of the most powerful technology companies in the world.
items.title: Former Enforcers Propose Ten Ways for States to Use Meta Settlement Funds

items.summary: In response to Edmund Goh's letter dated Oct 28 urging enforcement mechanisms for unresolved estate defects, the Building and Construction Authority explains that under the Building (Strata Management) Act, management corporations strata title (MCSTs) manage common property. It points owners toward Strata Management Guides covering water seepage, direct discussion with MCSTs or general meetings, and recourse through the independent Strata Titles Boards.
items.title: BCA Clarifies MCST Role in Resolving Estate Maintenance Disputes

items.summary: The MCST Association of Singapore, writing to respond to Edmund Goh's October 28 letter on enforcement mechanisms for unresolved estate defects, agrees that visual inspection alone is inadequate. It argues accountability must span five points: owners' duties under Section 63 of the Building (Strata Management) Act, managing agents complying with the BSMA, developers honouring a 12-month defects liability period, qualified persons meeting Section 9 of the Building Control Act, and main contractors building to approved plans. The association urges role-specific escalation protocols for all parties rather than targeting only managing agents.
items.title: MCST Association Urges Broader Accountability for Estate Defects

items.summary: Asian markets rose on Nov 9 after a volatile week weighed on tech stocks amid concerns over chip demand, US midterm results and rising interest rates. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan climbed 2%, while the dollar strengthened to its biggest gain in five months as Fed rate-hike bets grew. Analysts note dip-buying may be emerging ahead of key earnings reports.
items.title: Asian Stocks Recover as AI and Middle East Fears Ease

items.summary: China's producer price index rose 5.7% year on year in October, the National Bureau of Statistics said, its largest annual gain since June 2022 when it climbed 6.1%. Higher global oil prices pushed up costs for energy-intensive sectors. Consumer inflation eased to 0.7%, below expectations at 0.8%, as weak demand held spending down. Core CPI fell to 0.8% from 1.0%. Capital Economics expects producer-price deflation and 0.4% consumer inflation in 2027, while Pinpoint Asset Management's Zhang Zhiwei sees no rush for stimulus amid strong exports.
items.title: China's Factory-Gate Inflation Hits Fastest Pace in Nearly Four-and-a-Half Years

items.summary: Reporting from Data Center Alley in Ashburn and Loudoun County, Virginia, argues that opposition to data centers stems more from their large electricity demand than Big Tech's framing of it as a culture war. OpenAI's Chris Lehane described the conflict as public unease over affordability and corporate power, but activist Elena Schlossberg insists 'It was always about power.' The author notes average facilities draw 54 megawatts while AI-focused sites may reach 6,000 megawatts, often requiring private natural-gas turbines. Onsite generation strains communities and releases pollutants, prompting new state rules on transmission costs. While job fears and misinformation also fuel opposition, the article concludes that electricity constraints shape where future facilities will be built.
items.title: Data center backlash is really about electricity, not culture war

items.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla cannot build more than one car at a time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around. He argues the bottleneck is staff, not factory space or money. Half the executives he presented in 2023 have left; seven of the 14 named presenters no longer work for Tesla. Program-level leaders departed too, including Cybercab managers Victor Nechita and Mark Lupkey. Musk frames this as focus on autonomy, but Electrek notes Tesla has repeatedly promised self-driving without delivering at scale — NHTSA estimates its Robotaxi fleet at about 1,000 vehicles. The outlet concludes the company cannot sustain multiple programs and is getting harder to staff.
items.title: Musk Cites Talent Shortage as Tesla Trims Vehicle Programs

items.summary: On Monday, Anthropic unveiled Claude Fable 5.2 for coding, reasoning and agent tasks, plus Claude Mythos 5.2 restricted to approved cybersecurity and life-sciences research. Both generate outputs up to 30 per cent faster than the Claude 5.1 models and cost $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. The launch follows its October rollout of Claude Haiku 5.5 as Anthropic prepares for a planned IPO amid intensifying competition from OpenAI, Alphabet's Google and Meta Platforms.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Fable and Mythos Models Ahead of IPO

items.summary: The Guardian editorial asks why Donald Trump took no action after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, whom he was told may have passed intelligence to Beijing. It suggests his inaction reflected loyalty rather than the seriousness of a foreign-intelligence threat, and argues Congress has grounds to investigate whether the administration knowingly disregarded it.
items.title: Guardian editorial questions Trump's handling of Jensen Huang affair

items.summary: Columnist Nils Pratley argues Nvidia’s board should act quickly on leadership succession as it investigates Jensen Huang over an alleged honeytrap spy scandal. The article notes the 63-year-old boss holds a plain 3.6% shareholding, that no chair exists and that lead directors are set annually by independent directors. While investigators found “no reason to believe” national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, Trump called him “an honourable guy,” and Sequoia Capital’s Shaun Maguire said Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.
items.title: Nvidia board urged on succession amid spy probe

items.summary: Fans mobbed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Taipei and Seoul for autographs, illustrating the personal appeal behind his role as gatekeeper to chips that train models like ChatGPT. Analysts warn this dependence creates risk: after reports of a foreign intelligence probe linked to Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing, Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon called it hard not to read the news negatively. Dan Ives argued Jensen is unreplaceable and no successor exists on Nvidia's leadership bench.
items.title: Why Nvidia's Jensen Huang Is Indispensable to AI Race

items.summary: Speculation follows Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of infidelity about what may become one of the largest divorces in history. His net worth was reported at approximately $162.2 billion as of November 8, per Forbes. An equal division would give his wife Lori Huang roughly $81.1 billion.
items.title: Nvidia co-founder's divorce could yield wife a half-billion-dollar fortune

items.summary: Bloomberg reports Nvidia's Jensen Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, linked by a US memo to Chinese intelligence. An independent board inquiry launched; Nvidia says no harm to classified data is known. US and Singapore investigate Megaspeed chip exports to China.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Board Probe Over CEO China Espionage Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic is releasing two new models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, roughly 20% below the prior generation, according to CNBC. Anthropic said both scored higher than Claude Opus 5.5 on nearly all evaluated capabilities. The launch arrives as Anthropic prepares an IPO targeting a valuation between $1 trillion and $1.5 trillion.
items.title: Anthropic Cuts Claude Model Prices and Unveils Two New Versions

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell after its board began investigating longtime CEO Jensen Huang over whether his extramarital affair exposed the chipmaker to a foreign espionage operation. Though President Donald Trump backed him, reports that the woman involved had ties to Chinese intelligence intensified leadership worries: Huang has led Nvidia since 1993 with no clear successor. One analyst told Reuters staying on stanchied declines, warning of an ‘absolute bloodbath’ if he stepped down.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall Amid Spying Allegations Against Jensen Huang

items.summary: The article argues that AI agents may help people navigate bureaucratic tasks like paying fines or challenging tickets, potentially rebalancing power between customers and businesses. The author illustrates this with a personal example of using ChatGPT to respond to a $75 littering fine more easily than fighting it manually. However, the piece warns that companies might block such agents under claims about malicious bots, possibly leading to stricter identity requirements resembling financial services' know-your-customer checks. This could threaten online privacy and free expression. The author proposes anonymous credentials and user-controlled signals as alternatives, noting Coin Center's John Hancock Project is developing a proof of concept, co-authored with Ian Miers.
items.title: AI agents could free users from bureaucracy but risk privacy tradeoffs

items.summary: The authors find that advised retirees hold roughly two-thirds of their portfolios in equities, about 30 to 40 percentage points more than non-advised retirees. These holdings reflect active choices rather than inertia and adjust gradually after advisor switches.
items.title: Advisors Push Retirees Toward Higher Equity Holdings

items.summary: A Bayesian meta-analysis of 49 studies on poverty Graduation programs finds large gains in consumption, income, savings, assets, food security, mental health, and women's empowerment. Programs with larger transfers yield bigger effects but are not more cost-effective; newer programs (from 2016) show higher benefit-cost ratios than earlier ones. The authors hypothesize continuous sector-community learning drives the trend.
items.title: Meta-Analysis Finds Poverty Graduation Programs Improve Income and Well-being After Two Decades

items.summary: The Nvidia chief executive has admitted to a relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China. The item offers this as the lead, then frames what follows as an introduction to key players and how they fit into the story.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Relationship With Woman Suspected of Chinese Espionage

items.summary: Nvidia's share price fell after the company announced an investigation into reports that its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia stated Mr Huang admitted to staff about the matter. Shares of Nvidia and other major AI companies have sold off steadily since early October, raising fears of a bubble in the sector.
items.title: Nvidia Share Price Falls After CEO Investigation Into Foreign Intelligence Reports

items.summary: US stocks rose sharply on Monday even as Nvidia slumped about 6% amid a foreign-intelligence investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The S&P 500 gained roughly 2.4%, its biggest daily gain since April 8, helped by falling oil prices that eased inflation concerns and Trump downplaying renewed Iran strikes. Every major S&P sector rose; chipmakers surged broadly while Nvidia was the sole decliner in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which rebounded more than 6% after a steep weekly drop. Analysts at Morgan Stanley and UBS called last week's AI rout an overreaction, though fears of a December rate hike lingered ahead of October inflation data. Prices were live around 7:15am AEDT with firm closing figures pending.
items.title: Wall Street rallies as Nvidia falls over spy probe

items.summary: Dancing robots from Aigibot opened Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon, putting China's artificial intelligence on stage. Founder Paddy Cosgrave told an audience of up to 12,000 people that the future's superstars come from China rather than California. Chinese firms like Manus AI demonstrated new capabilities with a 30-second video built from just a 13-word prompt. The event runs amid US-China tensions over high-powered chip exports and Nvidia's probe into Jensen Huang.
items.title: Web Summit Lisbon Opens With Chinese AI Showcased Amid US-China Chip Tensions

items.summary: On Monday, China rejected allegations that Huang Le—also known as Alice Huang and reportedly involved with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—worked for Chinese intelligence. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the claim “nothing but smears against China,” repeating the statement when pressed about an explicit denial. The accusations prompted Nvidia to launch an independent investigation on Sunday, the same day its founder acknowledged infidelity; shares fell as much as 6% in premarket trading. Suspicions first emerged October 29 after The New York Times reported U.S. intelligence concluded Huang was passing information to Beijing. Evidence remains unpublicized, and her background details have not been verified by AFP or EL PAÍS.
items.title: China Rejects Spy Allegations Against Nvidia Businesswoman Amid Investigation

items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met with Apple Executive Chairman Tim Cook in Ankara on Monday, according to the Turkish Presidency. The meeting took place at the Presidential Complex and was not open to the press. In a statement posted on NSosyal, Erdogan said the two spoke about "the future of digital technology at the global level" and discussed Apple's support for Türkiye's digital application economy.
items.title: Erdogan Meets Apple's Tim Cook in Türkiye

items.summary: Carlos Silva Filho, a member of the UN Secretary-General's Advisory Board on Zero Waste and Brazilian environmental expert, told Anadolu that Brazil must accelerate implementation of its national circular economy strategy. Speaking at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, he said policies alone are insufficient without faster action and greater financing. Citing the Global Waste Management Outlook 2024 report he helped coordinate, Filho noted current global waste management costs an estimated $252 billion annually, projected to reach $640 billion by 2050 under a business-as-usual scenario, while a circular economy approach could yield a net annual gain of $108.5 billion. He added that zero-waste prevention and broader measures could cut emissions by up to 20%, praising Türkiye's Zero Waste initiative as a global model. The report figures are attributed to UNEP; Filho's estimates reflect his own assessment.
items.title: UN zero-waste adviser urges Brazil to speed Amazon protection

items.summary: Nvidia's share price fell 4.51% pre-market after the company announced its board launched an independent investigation into reports that founder and CEO Jensen Huang may have been targeted in a foreign intelligence effort. Nvidia said it has no reason to believe national security or its secrets were compromised, while China denied any spy plot, calling the allegations unsubstantiated.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Slides as Company Probes Claims CEO Was Foreign Intelligence Target

items.summary: At least 17 people died and 12 others were injured in an explosion at the Habas Demir Celik iron and steel plant near Izmir, western Turkey. Authorities said all victims were workers. The local governor said a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed around midday, dropping materials into a furnace below. Eyewitnesses reported the ground shaking as if from an earthquake. President Erdoğan confirmed deaths while investigations continued; Health Minister Kemal Memişoğlu raised the toll to 17 after one critically injured person died.
items.title: Turkey Steel Factory Blast Kills at Least 17 Workers

items.summary: Republican Thomas Massie refiled eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, citing an unauthorized war in Iran and strikes that killed over 200 people. The House has two days to act; removal would require a Senate majority. Meanwhile, Democrats weigh new congressional leadership after midterm gains.
items.title: Massie revives impeachment push against Hegseth amid Democratic leadership contest

items.summary: Jensen Huang disclosed on Sunday that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive whom American officials believe was a Chinese intelligence asset. The revelation has prompted Nvidia’s board to launch an independent investigation into whether national security or company secrets were compromised, though the board stated it has no reason to believe either was breached and will examine all available information. Reports trace concerns back to last year when the New York Times and Bloomberg questioned Megaspeed over possible diversion of chips to China; both Nvidia and Megaspeed denied wrongdoing. The affair coincided with Huang’s close relationship with President Trump, during which he secured concessions including export approvals in exchange for revenue shares. Experts say his access exposed US policy-making, making him valuable intelligence to America’s rivals.
items.title: Nvidia Chief Reveals Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy, Prompting Board Probe

items.summary: On Nov. 4, 2026, Peruvian customs and the National Forest and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) said they seized more than 3,000 tarantulas at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima, hidden in socks bound for Germany. The alleged traffickers—two German citizens and a Polish national—are facing criminal proceedings. SERFOR technician Cora Suárez described finding spiders from eggs to adults across five Peruvian regions. Sandra Altherr of the German NGO Pro Wildlife told Mongabay that because none of the species are CITES-protected, they could have been legally imported had they not been caught violating Peru's national law.
items.title: Peru Seizes Thousands of Tarantulas at Lima Airport

items.summary: The Paris prosecutor announced an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit of the Islamic Republic's ideological army (IRGC), over October attacks on French supermarket refrigerators. Analysts note the IRGC has expanded into cyber warfare in recent years.
items.title: Paris Prosecutor Opens Probe Into IRGC Cyber Unit Over Fridge Attacks

items.summary: British comedian Russell Brand was jailed Monday for more than 10 years over a series of sex offences including rape. Judge Joel Bennathan called him a 'sexual predator' whose fame had shielded him, adding that he acted with 'staggering arrogance'. The report is by France 24's Carys Garland.
items.title: Russell Brand Sentenced to Over Ten Years for Rape and Assault

items.summary:
On Monday, November 9, 2026, China launched the 29th group of satellites for its low-Earth-orbit satellite internet constellation from the Hainan commercial space launch site in Wenchang. A Long March-12 rocket blasted off at 4:24 a.m., placing the satellites into their preset orbit. Officials said this was the country's first single-core, 4-meter-class rocket and marked the 676th flight of the Long March series.

visual null},
items.title: China Launches 29th Group of LEO Internet Satellites on Long March-12

items.summary: A short trailer for a documentary titled 'The Sea We Call Home' describes how the sea has shaped local life, work and navigation across generations. It notes that some vessels carry fresh water while others follow ancient routes, and shows fishermen heading out as their families wait at home. The program is scheduled to begin airing on CGTN starting November 11.
items.title: CGTN Trailer Announces Documentary on Coastal Communities

items.summary: Fu Yuhua and Lu Chunxiang, now mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, wait for Su Biaowei to return from the sea. Their husbands and father went out on the same fishing boat more than half a century ago and neither came back. The women feature in "The Sea We Call Home," which begins airing November 11 on CGTN.
items.title: Two Women Await a Family Member's Return From Sea

items.summary: Inger Andersen, executive director of the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), argues that investing in climate adaptation is no longer optional. Citing UNEP's latest Adaptation Gap Report 2026: Ready?, she says international public adaptation finance reached only $28-32 billion in 2024, while developing countries need around $305 billion a year by 2035; even tripling current levels would cover no more than 30% of needs. Speaking as nations gather for the 31st UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, she warns that resilience is underfunded and losses mount, urging bold action now rather than paying far more later.
items.title: UNEP chief urges climate adaptation investment amid widening finance gap

items.summary: Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale School of Management told Tech Crunch that Jensen Huang's chances of keeping his Nvidia post are about a 50-50, citing the social psychologist Edwin Hollander's 1958 idiosyncrasy credits theory. Sonnenfeld said Huang earned goodwill over three decades but must show he was misled by an alleged intelligence operation before November earnings and congressional briefing. The outcome hinges on board confidence rather than founder status.
items.title: Yale expert weighs Jensen Huang's leadership survival amid scandal

items.summary: US President Donald Trump's close relationship with embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday, after Nvidia said its board was investigating whether the tech executive had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The inquiry followed New York Times reporting that Huang maintained a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom US officials believe passed information to China; Trump reportedly chose not to act on it. Nvidia shares fell to a seven-month low, and neither Washington nor the company immediately responded to Reuters.
items.title: Nvidia board probe deepens scrutiny of Trump-Huang ties

items.summary: An internal Nvidia investigation into reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was a target of foreign intelligence activity sent shares down 8% at Monday's start, per the item. The New York Times identified Alice Huang as a former Megaspeed International executive linked to China-linked information gathering; Beijing rejected the claims as a smear campaign. Analysts question whether India benefits indirectly: Sensex and Nifty posted negative returns over the past year but may gain from an anti-AI trade, with HSBC upgrading Indian stocks and Citi raising its 12-month target for the Nifty 50 to 50.
items.title: Nvidia probe sparks speculation on Indian markets

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India told some lenders they should change how they account for bond forwards contracts, worth billions across the industry. During in-person audits, RBI said such trades should use Level 3 inputs, which rely on a bank's own assumptions because value cannot be checked against market data. The classification can force banks to limit dividends and hold less regulatory capital. Banks are seeking a resolution with FIMMDA and Clearing Corp. of India Ltd., which did not respond to requests for comment. Figures were reported by people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified.
items.title: RBI Asks Banks to Revalue Bond Forwards Using Level 3 Inputs

items.summary: IIT Guwahati won the third edition of the Lam Research Challenge, an industry-led semiconductor systems engineering competition that drew more than 3,000 students from institutions across India. IIT Ropar took runner-up and NIT Calicut finished third. The top teams shared prize money worth ₹10 lakh, with select participants gaining internship opportunities at Lam Research.
items.title: IIT Guwahati Wins Lam Research Semiconductor Challenge

items.summary: A report says RBI's USD 239 billion net short position in the forward market, as of September 2026, may limit rupee appreciation despite recovering foreign portfolio investor inflows. IDFC First Bank said improving capital flows would be absorbed by the central bank to meet maturing buy-sell swaps. The report expects near-term gains if US-Iran tensions ease and AI stocks correct, but sustained strength faces headwinds from global competition for capital.
items.title: RBI Forward Short Position May Cap Rupee Gains

items.summary: Beijing dismissed allegations that it spied on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling them unsubstantiated and 'nothing but smears against China,' Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a press briefing. The episode could complicate the upcoming Xi-Trump summit set for next week in Shenzhen, amid concerns over trade ties and an AI market shaken by data center spending worries.
items.title: China Rejects Nvidia Spy Allegations as Baseless Smears Ahead of Xi-Trump Summit

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a government has wide powers to compulsorily retire an employee to improve administrative efficiency, and such a decision cannot be challenged on the ground that similarly placed colleagues were not retired. Upholding Chhattisgarh's retirement of five officers after two-tier scrutiny, Justices Manmohan and Shree Chandrashekhar held Article 311(2)'s 'hear before punish' principle does not apply, since compulsory retirement is neither punitive nor defamatory.
items.title: Supreme Court Affirms Broad Government Power for Compulsory Retirement

items.summary: Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali day in five years, with AQI reaching 376 at 4pm on Nov 8. It narrowly avoided its worst post-Diwali pollution day since records began, peaking at 370 before easing to 344 by 4pm. Gufran Beig of SAFAR and NIAS said Delhi was 'very lucky' this year rather than cleaner, attributing the relief to an unusual easterly wind shift from a cyclone and western disturbance that dispersed pollutants faster than usual. Anumita Roychowdhury of CSE warned the post-Diwali respite is more meteorological than evidence of pollution-control success, cautioning winter winds could return the familiar smog as Punjab farm fires spiked to 1,152 incidents on Nov 8.
items.title: Delhi's Worst Diwali Air in Five Years, Then a Meteorological Reprieve

items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered changes to the curriculum at US senior service colleges, arguing that future admirals and generals need education more focused on winning wars than academic theories. Announced during a speech at the Naval War College in Newport, Rhode Island, Hegseth said an 18-month review by his office revealed resistance to the Trump administration's push for change.
items.title: Hegseth Orders Military Schools to Focus on Victory Over Theory

items.summary: The Bombay High Court declined immediate relief in a plea by the Mithila Chhath Puja Sangh seeking permission to hold celebrations at Mumbai's Girgaon Chowpatty on November 15 and 16. A vacation bench of Justices Advait M Sethna and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale held that religious freedom under Article 25 remains subject to public order, morality and health. The organisers had sought an alternative venue, which the bench declined to address, leaving them free to pursue other legal remedies.
items.title: Bombay High Court Denies Chhath Puja Relief at Girgaon Chowpatty
